summary: Test membership in a short explicit set.
documentation: IN checks whether a value matches a member of a list or subquery. WHERE keeps rows where that comparison is true. When NULL participates, a nonmatching result can be unknown rather than false.
inputs: A left expression and list or single-column subquery.
returns: A membership truth value, potentially NULL.
caution: NOT IN with a NULL in its comparison set can yield surprising unknown results. Do not assume it behaves like an ordinary two-valued exclusion.
scenarios: Select orders in several active workflow states.
Report on a chosen set of branch offices.
Retrieve appointments assigned to selected staff IDs.
title: Collect active order states
problem: From orders(id INTEGER, status TEXT), return id and status where status is exactly pending or packed. Use default text comparison; exclude other or NULL statuses and order by id.
goal: Use IN or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: List both accepted statuses in one membership condition.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT or WITH query using the provided tables.
SELECT 1;
